central_result: A new exact reciprocity dictionary removes the large common physical root p*D from the arithmetic reciprocal modulus while preserving it in the congruence/difference quotient and in the true lcm. The remaining root phase has denominator g*d1, not p*D. This permits a genuine three-factor Cauchy/spectral route; the required spectral estimate is not present as an identified formal theorem in the fixed native package.

actual_dictionary.original_units: N1 coprime delta*v0; N2 coprime delta*w0. Hence g and d1 are coprime L, n1 coprime delta*v0, n2 coprime w0. Together with gcd(v0,w0)=1 and reduced-N coprimality these imply (g*d1*n2*v0) coprime (n1*w0) and (n1*L) coprime (g*d1).
actual_dictionary.difference_integer: Compatibility gives delta | (N1-N2). Since g coprime delta, delta | (d1*n1-n2) in Int. Put f=(d1*n1-n2)/delta in Int, so p*D*f=d1*n1-n2 exactly.
actual_dictionary.inverse_names: t=local CanonicalReciprocalPhase.wPhaseInverse (g*d1*n2*v0) (n1*w0); z=the same local inverse (n1*L) (g*d1); b=actual ComplexCRT.residue (p*v) (p*w) N1 N2 a.
actual_dictionary.exact_UnitAddCircle_identity: (b/L : UnitAddCircle)=(-a*z/(g*d1) : UnitAddCircle)+(a/(N1*L) : UnitAddCircle)+(a*f*t/(n1*w0) : UnitAddCircle). All casts and signed a,f remain explicit in the future source.
actual_dictionary.fourier_identity: For every signed integer h, Fourier of the actual residue is product of the three displayed Fourier factors. This combines the original three canonical factors by an exact equality; no phase is approximated away.
general_divisibility_proof: Set E=N1*b-a-a*f*g*d1*delta*v0*t. First delta*v0 divides E by the first original CRT congruence.
The inverse identity gives (g*d1*n2*v0)*t=1 mod(n1*w0). The second original CRT congruence modulo w0 then gives w0 | (b-a*d1*v0*t).
Using delta*f=d1*n1-n2, expand E=g*d1*n1*(b-a*d1*v0*t)+a*((g*d1*n2*v0)*t-1). Consequently n1*w0 divides E.
Also E=(N2*b-a)+g*delta*f*(b-a*d1*v0*t). Thus delta*w0 divides E.

As n1 coprime delta, combine the last two divisibilities after factoring common w0 to get delta*n1*w0 | E. Then combine delta*v0 | E and gcd(v0,n1*w0)=1 to get n1*L | E. This explicitly permits delta/w0 overlap; separate n1|E and L|E are insufficient.
Let j=E/(n1*L) in Int. Modulo g*d1, E=-a and n1*L is a unit, so j=-a*z mod(g*d1). Divide the exact E identity by g*d1*n1*L and reduce modulo one.
actual_dictionary.bounded_exact_control: 3714 valid small tuples, including composite delta, overlap delta with v0 or w0, nontrivial g/d1, signed a and f=0, passed exact Fraction mod-one equality. This is implementation control only; the preceding general divisibility proof is the mathematical justification.

If f=0 then N1=N2 and g=N1>=U>X^eta, contradiction. Thus this retained core has no f=0; the later frequency-collision k=0 remains a different nonempty contribution.

f_zero_sign_and_original_carrier.why_no_arbitrary_q_weight_extension: After substitution the original p-carrier, p-unit and dyadic endpoint indicators depend on f,N labels,D, not on the inner unfrozen gamma2 variable. remaining_regions_before_spectral.large_supported_part: d1 is not bounded by g. For d1>Ysupport, owned/native prime-support arithmetic produces a square divisor b^2|N1 with b^2>d1. Existing card_largeSquareDivisorSet_le_real gives a thin original N1 set. A same-p pair bound #thinN1*(2U/p+1), retaining its p congruence, then pays this region by a new whole-W plus SAME-MASK raw-zero argument, analogous to the submitted large-paired proof. This must be proved; native largeSupport aggregate without 1/p is not a drop-in outside payment.
remaining_regions_before_spectral.large_support_expected_scale: With #thinN1<=C U/sqrt(Ysupport), the paired count is <=C(U^2/(p*sqrt(Ysupport))+U/sqrt(Ysupport)). Multiply V/p for raw-zero (or 4V/p+1 times true subpower divisor cost for wholeW), then sum p and actual outside: X^2*(Ysupport^-1/2+(Q1/U)*Ysupport^-1/2) times fixed logs/subpower. Choosing subpower epsilon after eta pays Ysupport=X^eta. No new geometric hypothesis.
remaining_regions_before_spectral.small_root_freezing: On g,d1<=X^eta, q0=g*d1<=X^(2eta). The new root phase depends only on h,a,n1,L residues modulo q0 because it is -a*h*inverse(n1L)/q0. Freeze the finite residue labels BEFORE Cauchy; retain lambda_s restricted to its fixed residue class as an independent one-bounded sequence. Outer residue conditions may be dropped only after the positive square. This prevents arbitrary level-dependent b,c weights from entering the final spectral sum.
remaining_regions_before_spectral.small_multiplier: The remaining reciprocal inverse contains fixed A=g*d1. Combine Bvariable=A*n2*r1, Cvariable=n1*r2*s2. Positive extension from multiples of A to a full B box occurs only after Cauchy, costing an explicit fixed polynomial in A rather than replacing residue a by a variable modular representative. The main spectral numerator stays original integer a.
remaining_regions_before_spectral.small_D_allocations: For tail D<=X^eta, split each full product independently into D times a coprime residual pair, record divisor allocations between the original Q2 and Q3 slots, and retain actual product endpoint restrictions. Never call a theorem requiring small physical delta=pD. Any loss exponent from D,g,d1 allocations, residue freezing and unbalanced N scales must be given an explicit finite Cg before eta is selected.
remaining_regions_before_spectral.close_pairs: If reciprocal normalization needs |d1*n1-n2| separated from zero, first isolate the actual close-pair strip and pay it with congruent-pair counting plus the Q1/U gate. A denominator 1/(n1-n2) is never treated as uniformly smooth without this step.

three_scale_arithmetic_estimate_to_prove.large_a_not_erased: Keep the explicit 1+|a|/X through the fourth root: its power loss is kappa/4. The separate retained slow-phase variation costs 5kappa. Neither is relabelled as an arbitrarily small epsilon.

theorem MediumAtom.actualCRT_fourier_eq_canonicalPhases
    {B : ℕ} {sigma kappa c0 : ℝ} {d : MediumAtom}
    (hd : MediumAdmissible B sigma kappa c0 d)
    {l l' : (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) × ℕ}
    (hl : l ∈ d.complexRowLabels) (hl' : l' ∈ d.complexRowLabels)
    (hc : ComplexCRT.Compatible (complexFactorModulus l.1)
      (complexFactorModulus l'.1) l.2 l'.2) (h : ℤ) :
    let v := d.canonicalReciprocalData l l'
    let b := ComplexCRT.residue (complexFactorModulus l.1)
      (complexFactorModulus l'.1) l.2 l'.2 d.residue
    fourier h (((b : ℝ) /
      (complexFactorModulus l.1).lcm (complexFactorModulus l'.1) : ℝ) : UnitAddCircle) =
      fourier h (CanonicalReciprocalPhase.rootPhase v b d.residue) *
        fourier h (CanonicalReciprocalPhase.slowPhase v d.residue) *
          fourier h (CanonicalReciprocalPhase.reciprocalPhase v d.residue)
